footnote.body:
One question before the footnote half of this task is built. The phone-width half does not depend on it and goes ahead.

@jwildfire: what should the two links of the RBQM tab's footnote open?

- The design says the tab gets "the same footnote links as a chart: its docs and its test evidence", and the review behind it said "gsm's own documentation and the tab's test evidence".
- A chart's footnote links pages the docs site builds for that chart. The site builds no page for the RBQM tab: none that describes it, and none for its tests, which are recorded on every chart's evidence page with the rest of the app's.
- gsm's own documentation does exist, on another host: `https://gilead-public.github.io/gsm.kri/`. Linking it adds a fifth host to the ones the app's page names, in a link only, as bio.viz's site is today.

The choices as I see them:

1. One link, "gsm.kri documentation", to gsm's site, and no evidence link until the tab has a page. The least to build, and true today.
2. Two links: gsm's documentation, and for evidence the demo app's requirement matrix on GitHub (`requirements/demo-app.md`), where the tab's 53 rows name their tests. Nothing new to build, but the second link lands on a long table.
3. A page on the docs site for the RBQM tab (what it runs, what each metric needs, its tests), and the footnote links it. About half a day, and it is a page the design did not draw.
4. No footnote in 1.11.

I would build the first, and file the third as a follow-up.

---
This comment was drafted by Claude Code using Opus 5.5.

answer.body:
@jwildfire answered in the session on 2026-10-10, choosing from the four above: "One link, gsm.kri docs".

- Built on the branch `300-release-prep`: the RBQM tab ends with "RBQM: gsm.kri documentation", a link to https://gilead-public.github.io/gsm.kri/ that opens in a new tab, in the same line a chart's footnote uses. It is there before R and after a run, on the Overview page and on a metric's, and at 390 pixels.
- It merges with release prep (#300), in one pull request and one refresh of the evidence, after the check's four-job split (#292) is on dev.
- A docs page for the RBQM tab, the third choice, is filed as a follow-up on the hub.

---

demo_path.body:
Merged in https://github.com/jwildfire/safety.viz/pull/301 (dev at 0fe006b6). The required check passed on it.

- The test: `tests/demo-path/demo-path.spec.js`, run by `npm run demo-path` at 1,280 by 720 pixels with real R. It fails on a console error, a page error, a failed request or an answer of 400 or more.
- Its passing run against the deployed dev demo (published from d97ac34), on GitHub's runner: https://github.com/jwildfire/safety.viz/actions/runs/38058471721 . No console error and no failed request.
- The nine screenshots are in [`docs/evidence/basic-app/demo-path/`](https://github.com/jwildfire/safety.viz/tree/dev/docs/evidence/basic-app/demo-path). They are from a second passing run of the same test against the same deployed demo, on a Mac a minute later: the GitHub run kept its own nine as its `demo-path` artifact, and a session may not download a file without your word.
- The path it walks, in order, which is yours to change: the app opens on the pilot study; the Adverse Event Explorer is opened; the app's status label is opened and closed; the Hepatic ALT Waterfall's Experimental label is opened; the Cross-tabulation starts R and shows a statistic; the RBQM tab runs 3 of 8 metrics on the pilot study; the RBQM demo study is chosen on the Data tab, whose card reads "This data supports 8 of 8 metrics."; the RBQM tab runs its eight metrics with no second press, and one metric's page is opened.
- It is apart from the required check, since it walks a published site and not the commit under test. The `demo-path` workflow runs it from the Actions tab, from a `demo-path` event a session can send, and on a pull request that changes the walk.
- You can now have the whole keynote path walked on the deployed demo in about half a minute, and be told if any step of it breaks.

---
This comment was drafted by Claude Code using Opus 5.5.

status.body:
Three things the build of the status ladder turned up. Each is built as the design says, so nothing waits on these, but each is a statement about status, so they are yours to rule on. The release candidate is the natural place.

- The Hepatic Explorer's migration view loses its mark. The design retires the banner drawn inside that view, and the chart as a whole is Exploratory, so in the app and on the docs site nothing now says the view is still moving. Its clinical guide still calls the view Experimental. If you want it marked: the Hepatic Explorer can show the status label, Experimental, while that view is open. That would be a seventh thing below Exploratory.
- The Time-to-Event Explorer's reason is one sentence, from the design's table: "Experimental until an external clinical review confirms its Kaplan–Meier estimates." The mockup's panel shows a second sentence, "Its curves, intervals and at-risk counts may change after that review." I shipped the table's, since the requirement names the table. Say if you want the second sentence back.
- The Participant Profile carries its label on its own page in the app, but not when it opens in the rail beside another chart, where the open chart's card is Exploratory and shows none. That is unchanged from today, when the profile carried no mark anywhere in the app. If you want it marked there, the rail's heading can carry the label.

One wording change of mine: a Prototype's panel is headed "Patient Journey Explorer is a prototype", not "is prototype".

---
This comment was drafted by Claude Code using Opus 5.5.
